sources.title: SQLite isolation
sources.released_version_or_commit: SQLite official living documentation; WAL supported since 3.7.0 (2010-07-21)
sources.locator: Isolation between connections; WAL; Summary
sources.observed_operation: Read official isolation behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_or_exception: Separate connections see committed transactions; WAL read txn sees stable snapshot; rollback mode is current default; exception is shared cache plus read_uncommitted.
sources.applicability: Database-specific example of snapshot semantics; target DB is unknown.
sources.limits: DB snapshots do not pin external files.

sources.title: SQLite Online Backup API
sources.locator: Sections 1, 1.1, 3, 3.1
sources.observed_operation: Read online backup and running DB example.
sources.governing_condition_default_or_exception: Incremental API releases read locks between steps; successful copy is snapshot from commencement; source writes can restart steps.
sources.applicability: Use only if target uses SQLite; alternative for point-in-time database view.
sources.limits: Not a portable project archive; may include unrelated data.

sources.title: PostgreSQL transaction isolation
sources.locator: 13.2.2 Repeatable Read, lines 90-104
sources.observed_operation: Read repeatable-read semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_or_exception: Repeatable Read sees data committed before transaction start and successive reads see same snapshot; same guarantee is DB-specific.
sources.applicability: Example if target DB is PostgreSQL; supports avoiding independent paged reads as consistency guarantee.
sources.limits: Do not generalize to other DBs or cross-store files.

sources.title: RFC 8259 JSON
sources.locator: Sections 4, 8.1, 9, 10
sources.observed_operation: Read JSON encoding/interoperability.
sources.governing_condition_default_or_exception: External JSON MUST be UTF-8; keys SHOULD be unique; parser may limit document size/depth/number/string ranges.
sources.applicability: Structured text records; NDJSON is a line-oriented application convention, not defined by this RFC.
sources.limits: No product schema or identifier rules.

sources.title: RFC 3339 timestamps
sources.released_version_or_commit: RFC 3339, July 2002; RFC Editor says updated by RFC 9557
sources.locator: Sections 4.1-4.4 and 5.6
sources.observed_operation: Read instant/offset semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_or_exception: Timestamp denotes an instant with UTC relationship; -00:00 means local offset unknown and differs from Z/+00:00; unqualified local time is not an interoperable instant.
sources.applicability: Use for actual instants; preserve date-only values separately and named time zone for local schedules.
sources.limits: Do not invent timezone semantics for naive dates.

sources.title: PKWARE ZIP APPNOTE
sources.observed_operation: Read streaming descriptor, ZIP64, central directory and end records.
sources.governing_condition_default_or_exception: Data descriptors support streaming; central directory/end records complete archive; ZIP64 expands fields when classic limits are too small.
sources.applicability: Compare stream-to-destination ZIP64 with folder and tar/PAX outputs.
sources.limits: Final archive structure alone does not prove record coverage/authenticity.

sources.title: GNU tar manual
sources.locator: Sections 8/8.3.5/8.3.6, 9, Appendix E
sources.observed_operation: Read archive format comparison.
sources.governing_condition_default_or_exception: ustar limits names, links and file sizes (<8 GiB); POSIX/PAX is more flexible but some older tools have issues; entries are sequential.

sources.title: SQLite Online Backup API
sources.version_or_commit: Rolling official documentation; no release version identified
sources.locator: Overview; sqlite3_backup_init/step/finish; Online Backup API details
sources.observed_operation: Online Backup API creates a database copy; repeated step calls copy bounded page batches.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The destination represents the source database as of copy commencement when the backup completes. Each step briefly read-locks the source, allowing other connections to continue; copying the raw database file is not equivalent and can block writers or risk corruption under interruption. The guarantee covers the SQLite database, not associated filesystem blobs. Under concurrent writes through other connections, the backup may restart; frequent restarts can prevent it from completing.
sources.applicability: Conditional mechanism for a SQLite database only; account for restart/starvation and separately pin or validate external blobs.
sources.critic_checked_locator: Overview; online-copy snapshot; §§3.1–3.2, concurrent writes and restart risk
sources.critic_observation_and_condition: The API can produce a database snapshot; incremental copying releases locks between steps. Writes from other handles may restart copying, and sufficiently frequent restarts can prevent completion. Database pages only; not sidecar blobs.

sources.title: SQLite Isolation
sources.version_or_commit: Rolling official documentation; no release version identified
sources.locator: Isolation between database connections; read transactions; read_uncommitted exception
sources.observed_operation: Describes visibility and isolation for concurrent SQLite connections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A read transaction sees a stable snapshot; commits from other connections remain invisible until a later transaction. Dirty reads are possible only with shared cache plus PRAGMA read_uncommitted; the default is off. Rollback-journal writes can block readers.
sources.applicability: Defines record snapshot expectations for a SQLite-backed export; not attachments outside the DB.
sources.critic_observation_and_condition: A read transaction is stable; dirty reads across connections require shared cache plus read_uncommitted, which defaults off.

sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
sources.version_or_commit: Rolling official documentation; no release version identified
sources.locator: Concurrency; checkpointing; WAL limitations
sources.observed_operation: Explains WAL readers/writers and snapshot behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Readers can continue against a stable snapshot while a writer appends to WAL; a reader’s snapshot predates later commits. WAL relies on shared memory and is not suitable when participating processes are on different machines.
sources.applicability: SQLite implementation detail only; export may run concurrently with writes but must hold a well-defined read view.
sources.critic_observation_and_condition: WAL readers retain a snapshot while writers append; WAL requires processes on one host and does not work over a network filesystem.

ZIP64 supports large entry sizes/counts/offsets. Readers must handle descriptors with or without a signature. ZIP defines container mechanics, not application schema or universal reader interoperability.

sources.critic_observation_and_condition: Data descriptors support streaming; central-directory and end records follow members. ZIP64 extends size/count/offset fields. Container rules do not establish extractor compatibility.

sources.title: The JSON Data Interchange Format
sources.locator: §4 objects; §6 numbers; §8.1 UTF-8
sources.observed_operation: Defines JSON interoperability requirements and recommendations.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Names within an object SHOULD be unique because duplicate-name receiver behavior varies. Inter-system JSON must be UTF-8. Numeric precision/interoperability is limited for large integers, so opaque identifiers should be strings.
sources.applicability: Machine-readable record encoding and stable ID representation.
sources.critic_observation_and_condition: Unique object names are a SHOULD; inter-system JSON uses UTF-8; exact integer interoperability is limited to the commonly supported binary64 range.

sources.title: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.version_or_commit: RFC 3339, 2002-07; updated by RFC 9557
sources.observed_operation: Defines an Internet profile for timestamps representing instants with an offset.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Offset-bearing timestamps identify instants; RFC 3339 is not a typed date-only or floating-local-time representation. Lexical precision/fractional digits and source semantics still need a contract.
sources.applicability: Represent instants; do not coerce date-only values into UTC midnight.
sources.critic_observation_and_condition: A date-time combines full-date, time and offset; this is not a complete type system for floating local or date-only values.

sources.title: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps with Additional Information (IXDTF)
sources.version_or_commit: RFC 9557, 2024-04; updates RFC 3339
sources.locator: §2–§4 time-zone annotation; limitations/security considerations
sources.observed_operation: Adds optional time-zone annotations to RFC 3339 timestamps.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A numeric offset and a time-zone identifier convey different facts. Zone rules may change; IXDTF does not define a general floating-local-time or date-only type, nor guarantee future local wall time semantics by itself.
sources.applicability: Preserve zone identity where source meaning requires it; retain raw source values and model date-only/local/instant distinctions explicitly.
sources.critic_checked_locator: RFC 9557 §§2–4 zone annotations and evolving zone rules
sources.critic_observation_and_condition: Offset and zone identifier convey different facts; named-zone rules can change. It does not define every date-only/floating value needed by an application.

sources.title: Universally Unique IDentifiers (UUIDs)
sources.locator: §4 UUID format; §6.5 name-based UUIDs and mutable names
sources.observed_operation: Defines UUID layouts and generation methods.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A UUID is a 128-bit identifier format, not a mandate to replace source identifiers. Name-based UUID inputs should not be mutable natural names if identity must remain stable.
sources.applicability: Preserve existing source IDs and namespace/type; generated IDs only by explicit import contract.
sources.critic_observation_and_condition: UUID generation is optional; it does not require replacing source identifiers, and mutable names are not stable identity inputs.

sources.title: JSON Schema Core
sources.version_or_commit: JSON Schema Draft 2020-12
sources.locator: §8 vocabularies and dialect; references; schema identification
sources.observed_operation: Defines schema dialect/vocabulary and reference processing.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A schema must identify its dialect; remote references create availability and integrity dependencies unless bundled or prohibited. Schema documents validate shape only to the extent their vocabularies/validator implement those semantics.
sources.applicability: Pin and bundle a local schema dialect; define unknown-field policy separately.
sources.critic_checked_locator: JSON Schema Core: dialect, references and bundling
sources.critic_observation_and_condition: The $schema keyword identifies dialect; referenced resources must be available to validators. Bundling is a recognized transport mechanism.

sources.title: SQLite Online Backup API
sources.version_or_commit: Rolling official documentation; no release version identified
sources.locator: Overview; sqlite3_backup_init/step/finish; Online Backup API details
sources.observed_operation: Online Backup API creates a database copy; repeated step calls copy bounded page batches.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The destination represents the source database as of copy commencement when the backup completes. Each step briefly read-locks the source, allowing other connections to continue; copying the raw database file is not equivalent and can block writers or risk corruption under interruption. The guarantee covers the SQLite database, not associated filesystem blobs.
sources.applicability: Use if the tracker database is SQLite; identify storage backend before selecting this mechanism.

sources.title: SQLite Isolation
sources.version_or_commit: Rolling official documentation; no release version identified
sources.locator: Isolation between database connections; read transactions; read_uncommitted exception
sources.observed_operation: Describes visibility and isolation for concurrent SQLite connections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A read transaction sees a stable snapshot; commits from other connections remain invisible until a later transaction. Dirty reads are possible only with shared cache plus PRAGMA read_uncommitted; the default is off. Rollback-journal writes can block readers.
sources.applicability: Defines record snapshot expectations for a SQLite-backed export; not attachments outside the DB.

sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
sources.version_or_commit: Rolling official documentation; no release version identified
sources.locator: Concurrency; checkpointing; WAL limitations
sources.observed_operation: Explains WAL readers/writers and snapshot behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Readers can continue against a stable snapshot while a writer appends to WAL; a reader’s snapshot predates later commits. WAL relies on shared memory and is not suitable when participating processes are on different machines.
sources.applicability: SQLite implementation detail only; export may run concurrently with writes but must hold a well-defined read view.

sources.title: rusqlite backup implementation

sources.applicability: Version-pinned implementation evidence, not a guarantee for another rusqlite version or backend.

sources.version_or_commit: Version 6.3.10, FINAL, revised 2022-11-01
sources.observed_operation: Specifies ZIP member records, streaming data descriptors, central directory/end records, ZIP64 metadata, and optional application manifests.

sources.title: SQLite Online Backup API
sources.version_or_commit: Rolling official documentation; page last updated 2025-11-13T07:12:58Z
sources.locator: Overview; sqlite3_backup_init/step/finish; §§3.1–3.2 concurrent-write restart risk
sources.observed_operation: Online Backup API creates a database snapshot; incremental step calls copy bounded page batches while allowing other connections to use the source between steps.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: When completed, destination is a consistent, up-to-date snapshot. A write from another connection while the incremental API sleeps usually restarts backup; repeated restarts can prevent completion indefinitely. Each step briefly read-locks the source. The guarantee covers only SQLite database pages, not associated filesystem blobs.
sources.applicability: Conditional on SQLite; set bounded retry/time policy and fail visibly if it is exhausted; separately pin or validate external blobs.
sources.critic_checked_locator: Overview; online-copy snapshot; §§3.1–3.2, concurrent writes and restart risk
sources.critic_observation_and_condition: The API can produce a database snapshot; incremental copying releases locks between steps. Writes from other handles may restart copying, and sufficiently frequent restarts can prevent completion. Database pages only; not sidecar blobs.

sources.title: SQLite Online Backup API
sources.version_or_commit: Rolling official documentation; no release version identified
sources.locator: Overview; sqlite3_backup_init/step/finish; Online Backup API details
sources.observed_operation: Online Backup API creates a database copy; repeated step calls copy bounded page batches.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The destination represents the source database as of copy commencement when the backup completes. Each step briefly read-locks the source, allowing other connections to continue; copying the raw database file is not equivalent and can block writers or risk corruption under interruption. The guarantee covers the SQLite database, not associated filesystem blobs. Under concurrent writes through other connections, the backup may restart; frequent restarts can prevent it from completing.
sources.applicability: Conditional mechanism for a SQLite database only; account for restart/starvation and separately pin or validate external blobs.
sources.critic_checked_locator: Overview; online-copy snapshot; §§3.1–3.2, concurrent writes and restart risk
sources.critic_observation_and_condition: The API can produce a database snapshot; incremental copying releases locks between steps. Writes from other handles may restart copying, and sufficiently frequent restarts can prevent completion. Database pages only; not sidecar blobs.

sources.title: SQLite Isolation
sources.version_or_commit: Rolling official documentation; no release version identified
sources.locator: Isolation between database connections; read transactions; read_uncommitted exception
sources.observed_operation: Describes visibility and isolation for concurrent SQLite connections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A read transaction sees a stable snapshot; commits from other connections remain invisible until a later transaction. Dirty reads are possible only with shared cache plus PRAGMA read_uncommitted; the default is off. Rollback-journal writes can block readers.
sources.applicability: Defines record snapshot expectations for a SQLite-backed export; not attachments outside the DB.
sources.critic_observation_and_condition: A read transaction is stable; dirty reads across connections require shared cache plus read_uncommitted, which defaults off.

sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
sources.version_or_commit: Rolling official documentation; no release version identified
sources.locator: Concurrency; checkpointing; WAL limitations
sources.observed_operation: Explains WAL readers/writers and snapshot behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Readers can continue against a stable snapshot while a writer appends to WAL; a reader’s snapshot predates later commits. WAL relies on shared memory and is not suitable when participating processes are on different machines.
sources.applicability: SQLite implementation detail only; export may run concurrently with writes but must hold a well-defined read view.
sources.critic_observation_and_condition: WAL readers retain a snapshot while writers append; WAL requires processes on one host and does not work over a network filesystem.

sources.applicability: Represent instants; do not coerce date-only values into UTC midnight.
sources.critic_observation_and_condition: A date-time combines full-date, time and offset; this is not a complete type system for floating local or date-only values.

sources.applicability: Preserve zone identity where source meaning requires it; retain raw source values and model date-only/local/instant distinctions explicitly.
sources.critic_checked_locator: RFC 9557 §§2–4 zone annotations and evolving zone rules
sources.critic_observation_and_condition: Offset and zone identifier convey different facts; named-zone rules can change. It does not define every date-only/floating value needed by an application.

sources.applicability: Preserve existing source IDs and namespace/type; generated IDs only by explicit import contract.
sources.critic_observation_and_condition: UUID generation is optional; it does not require replacing source identifiers, and mutable names are not stable identity inputs.

sources.title: SQLite FTS5 Extension
sources.version_or_commit: Living official SQLite documentation accessed 2026-10-12; contentless-delete tables documented since SQLite 3.43.0; shipped application runtime remains unknown.
sources.locator: Sections 2.1, 3, 4.3.1–4.3.4, 4.4.1–4.4.4, 6.12–6.13; FTS build availability, query grammar, Unicode61/trigram, contentless and contentless-delete operations, external-content synchronization, rebuild and secure-delete.
sources.observed_operation: Reopened the official FTS5 documentation at the tokenizer, table-mode, rebuild and secure-delete sections; checked the 3.43.0 contentless-delete condition, ordinary contentless UPDATE/DELETE restrictions, all-columns UPDATE rule, rebuild limitation, tokenizer defaults and deleted-term retention.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: unicode61 is the default and based on Unicode 6.1; letter/number/private-use runs are tokens, punctuation/space separate, and Latin diacritics are removed by default. Ordinary contentless tables do not support ordinary UPDATE/DELETE; their special delete command uses original indexed values and rowid. Since SQLite 3.43.0, contentless-delete tables support DELETE and INSERT OR REPLACE, and UPDATE only when all user-defined columns are supplied; they do not support the special delete command. External-content data is in the same database and synchronization is caller responsibility. Rebuild deletes/recreates the whole index and is unavailable for contentless tables. FTS5 postings may retain deleted terms until merge unless secure-delete is enabled.
sources.applicability: Primary source for conditional FTS5 design, tokenizer language limits, contentless CRUD and rebuild decisions, and at-rest posting caveat. Verify the actual runtime/build and tokenizer/index mode before implementation.

sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
sources.version_or_commit: Living official SQLite documentation; WAL available since SQLite 3.7.0.
sources.locator: Sections 1, 2, 2.1–2.3; concurrency, checkpointing, filesystem and attached-database conditions.
sources.observed_operation: Reopened official WAL documentation and checked reader/writer concurrency, one-writer limit, same-host/network-filesystem condition, checkpoint behavior and multi-database atomicity note.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WAL allows readers and a writer concurrently, but there is still only one writer at a time. Processes must use the database on one host; WAL does not work over a network filesystem. Transactions changing multiple attached database files are atomic per file but not across the set under WAL; long readers can hold back checkpoint progress.
sources.applicability: Relevant only if the target notebook or index uses SQLite/WAL; supports measuring same-database edit contention and keeping the canonical outbox durable across a separate index commit.

sources.title: SQLite FTS5 official manual
sources.version_or_commit: Living official manual; no manual revision/commit was exposed. Feature-specific release floor is recorded separately in S02.
sources.locator: Sections 2, 3, 4.3, 4.4, 5, 6.7, 6.12, 6.15, 6.16; especially query syntax, unicode61/trigram, external-content tables/pitfalls, delete/rebuild/integrity-check, secure-delete.
sources.observed_operation: Opened and read the official manual sections for build conditions, query grammar, tokenizers, external/contentless tables, synchronization, rebuild, integrity checking, and deletion handling.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: FTS5 may be compiled in or loaded as an extension. Default tokenizer is unicode61 (Unicode 6.1, Latin diacritic removal); default FTS storage copies content unless content= is specified. External-content tables read source columns from the named same-database object and require the app to keep postings synchronized. Contentless-delete starts in SQLite 3.43.0. FTS5 REBUILD requires an external content source and is unavailable for contentless tables. External-content integrity comparison requires rank=1. Trigram under-three-character terms miss and some patterns scan. Tokens >32768 bytes are silently truncated. secure-delete defaults off; FTS postings may retain deleted terms until merge unless both FTS/core settings are used.
sources.applicability: Directly governs SQLite candidate semantics, storage duplication, query grammar, tokenizer limits, and recovery design. Actual packaged SQLite feature set is unknown; do not assume FTS5 or 3.43.0+.
sources.evidence_summary: Official source for FTS5 behavior and exceptions. It shows both why SQLite can be suitable for an embedded notebook and why async updates, content retention, tokenization, and rebuild design must be explicit.

final_author_recheck.operation: Re-opened official FTS5 manual at contentless-delete, external-content, and REBUILD passages.
final_author_recheck.result: Final wording specifies a fresh generation from canonical notes for the contentless-delete option and keeps external-content REBUILD tied to its configured content table.

sources.title: Accessing files from the macOS App Sandbox
sources.version_commit: Living Apple Foundation/macOS documentation; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Persist file access with security-scoped URL bookmarks; Access files related to documents with document-relative bookmarks.
sources.observed_operation: Inspected Apple search-indexed documentation and the linked page. Direct page requires JavaScript, so the indexed documentation text was used.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Security-scoped bookmarks preserve user-granted access across app exits; sandbox entitlements are required. Resolution reports stale bookmark state, which should be replaced with newly created bookmark data. Resolve, start access, use, then stop access. Document-relative bookmark data can be stored in the project document and resolved by a process with access to that project.
sources.applicability: Strong macOS sandbox access adapter and project-relative permission mechanism; platform-specific and not a cross-platform identity or file-search service.

sources.title: URLByResolvingBookmarkData:options:relativeToURL:bookmarkDataIsStale:error:
sources.version_commit: Living Apple Foundation API documentation; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Parameters relativeURL, isStale; Discussion; Return Value.
sources.observed_operation: Inspected Apple search-indexed API documentation.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: For security-scoped app bookmark resolution pass nil relative URL; for document-scoped bookmarks use the absolute path of the owning document. isStale == true calls for new bookmark data. Resolution fails if the original item cannot be located or its volume cannot be mounted; last-known path may be read from bookmark data. Security scope additionally requires entitlements and start/stop access calls.
sources.applicability: Explains stale and offline/removable-volume states; bookmark failure should lead to visible recovery, not deletion of the record.

sources.title: Distributed Link Tracking and Object Identifiers
sources.version_commit: Microsoft Learn, last updated 2021-12-30.
sources.locator: Object Identifiers; Link Tracking Features; Link Tracking Functionality; Link Tracking Limitations (lines 31-104).
sources.observed_operation: Opened the Microsoft Learn implementation overview.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: NTFS object IDs are optional; rename/backup/restore preserve them but copies do not. Shell/OLE tracking also uses path/name/creation-date/size heuristics and can be slow or fail. System client/server services mediate tracking; cross-volume behavior has domain and timing conditions. Only NTFS 3.0+ is supported; FAT loses tracking; removable-media links are not maintained; newly connected NTFS volume may not be recognized until reboot.
sources.applicability: Useful alternative for Windows users, but too narrow and system-dependent to be required or trusted as the cross-platform core.

sources.title: inode(7) — Linux manual page
sources.version_commit: Linux man-pages living documentation; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: st_dev and st_ino descriptions, lines 24-43.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the Linux man-pages page and inspected the device/inode fields.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: st_ino is unique only within one filesystem; pair it with st_dev to identify the filesystem context. The same inode number may exist on another filesystem.
sources.applicability: Linux live equality hint while the relevant filesystem is mounted; do not treat as project-portable or universal permanent identity.

sources.title: XDG Desktop Portal Documents interface

Deleting a portal entry removes access entry, not the underlying file. Version 5 adds host-path lookup.

sources.title: RFC 8089: The file URI Scheme

sources.title: ReadDirectoryChangesW function (winbase.h)
sources.version_commit: Microsoft Learn, last updated 2022-09-15.
sources.locator: Parameters bWatchSubtree; Remarks on buffer overflow and ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR (lines 61-62, 114-130).
sources.observed_operation: Opened the Microsoft Learn API page.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Subtree watch is a caller option. If the notification buffer overflows, its entire contents are discarded; zero bytes or ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR requires enumerating the directory/subtree to recompute changes. Some network redirectors/file systems may not support the operation.
sources.applicability: Windows watcher can be a best-effort refresh signal for chosen roots; it is not a durable, lossless locator database.

sources.title: inotify(7) — Linux manual page
sources.version_commit: Living Linux man-pages; page version not specified.
sources.locator: DESCRIPTION, rename event examples, Limitations and caveats, Dealing with rename() events.
sources.observed_operation: Searched and inspected full indexed manual text; direct page fetch timed out.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Directory watches are not recursive; move-from/move-to pairing is racy and may lack a destination event when outside the watched set; queue overflow drops events; remote network filesystem changes are not reported; watched unmount removes watches.
sources.applicability: Linux watcher is a best-effort hint for currently monitored directories and cannot justify unvalidated persistent path rewriting.

sources.title: Loro List and Movable List
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs, no version pinned; JS/WASM examples; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Heading List and Movable List, lines 71-76 and 113-166.
sources.observed_operation: Shows List insert/delete, MovableList set/move, two replicas making concurrent moves and importing updates; both converge to one deterministic position, with the higher PeerID's move winning in the example.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: List is for insert/delete; simulating move with delete+insert can yield duplicate logical elements under concurrent edits. MovableList has native move/set but costs more; docs estimate about 80% slower encode/decode and 50% more memory for insert/delete-only workloads.
sources.applicability: Direct fit for ordered cue reordering; convergence does not present both move intents for human choice.

sources.title: Loro Cursor and Stable Positions
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs, no version pinned; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Heading Cursor, lines 70-80 and examples 81-110.
sources.observed_operation: Separately storable cursor identifies a position in Text/List/MovableList; after insert/delete, it resolves to an updated position. Docs demonstrate cursors for comment ranges.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Integer indexes are unstable. When a referenced element is deleted, Loro recalculates the position by replaying relevant history and updates cursor metadata to refer to present elements; longer replay can cost more. JS offsets use UTF-16.
sources.applicability: Useful for optional text-range comments; cue-level comments should use an explicit cue_id rather than sequence indexes.

sources.title: Loro Sync
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs, no version pinned; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Real-time Collaboration and Sync Strategies, lines 77-120; Import Status/Pending Operations, lines 184-200.
sources.observed_operation: Exports updates from a peer version vector and imports them; same state is reached for the same updates independent of order/duplicates. Import status exposes pending causal dependencies. Regular child containers independently created under one Map key can hide a value; docs recommend ensure_mergeable_* for shared logical keys.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Convergence assumes peers eventually receive the same update set. Non-empty pending ranges mean required dependencies are missing. Conflicting regular child containers under one map key do not both appear as values.
sources.applicability: Supports offline update exchange, durable outbox/relay design, schema initialization, and explicit missing-range recovery.

sources.title: Loro Rust LoroDoc API and source
sources.version_or_commit: Rust crate loro 1.16.2, exact version page; docs.rs latest resolved to 1.16.2 during research.
sources.locator: LoroDoc import/export, import_batch, try_get_movable_list, checkout/frontiers methods; matching implementation index at https://docs.rs/loro/1.16.2/src/loro/lib.rs.html#3339.
sources.observed_operation: Rust API imports/exports snapshots and incremental updates; import_batch accepts arbitrary order; ImportStatus reports pending dependencies; checkout reads a selected frontier; Rust wrapper exposes get_movable_list and recoverable try_get_movable_list.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Library does not implement a network protocol or local storage; caller owns those. Pending import is incomplete until dependencies arrive. Checkout detaches state; reattach/checkout_to_latest before ordinary editing.
sources.applicability: Native Rust fit for Rust/Slint; evidence does not prove UI integration, Windows packaging, or team-scale performance.

sources.title: Loro PeerID Management
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs, no version pinned; Rust API warning corroborated by S04; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Quick Reference and Automatic/Manual assignment, lines 75-103; Rust API set_peer_id pitfall in S04.
sources.observed_operation: Default creates a random PeerID per LoroDoc instance/session, including when loading the same document again; operation identity is (PeerID, counter).
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Never reuse PeerID across concurrent writers; duplicate IDs can yield conflicting operation IDs and document corruption. Manual fixed IDs require strict single-writer ownership.
sources.applicability: Requires process/session identity policy and duplicate-writer/recovery tests; relay does not remove this invariant.

sources.title: Loro import lock-order issue and fix PR
sources.version_or_commit: Issue opened 2026-04-23; reproducer used loro-crdt@1.11.1, @loro-extended/repo@6.0.0-beta.0 and adapter-webrtc@6.0.0-beta.0; linked PR #958 merged 2026-04-25 as commit 0977ad1. Report mentions main commit 7dfda879.
sources.locator: Issue #957 summary/repro, lines 138-177 and 208-239; PR #958 merged-status and summary, lines 130-173 and 251-264.
sources.observed_operation: A user report observed lock-order panics on imports under a connected Node/WebRTC adapter. Merged PR #958 changed len_ops() to read a cached op count instead of re-locking OpLog, kept the count synchronized through imports/rollback, and added regression coverage.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Specific WASM/Node/third-party WebRTC adapter and high multi-document/two-tab load, not a Rust-native defect claim or proof of a present bug.
sources.applicability: Justifies testing chosen adapter with concurrent import, reconnect, load, and failure paths rather than validating only core merges.

sources.title: Automerge conflict behavior
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs; JS-oriented example, no version pinned; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Conflict semantics, lines 58-112.
sources.observed_operation: Concurrent assignments to one property yield a deterministic displayed winner and retained alternatives accessible through getConflicts; a later assignment clears the conflict.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Winner ordering uses operation IDs rather than wall-clock time. Alternatives stay inspectable only until code assigns the property again.
sources.applicability: Credible local-first/Rust alternative; UI must inspect/persist conflicts before overwriting and cannot treat LWW as approval.

sources.title: Automerge Lists
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs; JS examples; no version pinned; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Fine-grained update guidance, lines 97-134.
sources.observed_operation: Docs recommend updating list IDs and entity-map entries directly rather than replacing an entire nested object, because whole-object replacement conflicts at the containing property.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Fine-grained edits help disjoint concurrent operations merge; they do not define a first-class move or stage-staff decision workflow.
sources.applicability: Relevant to cue ID list plus entity map if Automerge is chosen.

sources.title: Automerge Rust sync protocol
sources.version_or_commit: Official Rust API docs, generated version not exposed in captured page; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Module description, lines 17-25.
sources.observed_operation: Each synchronizing peer keeps per-peer sync state and exchanges generated/received messages in a loop.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Protocol assumes a reliable in-order stream between peers.
sources.applicability: Transport/relay must satisfy or wrap that stream contract.

sources.title: Yjs Offline Support
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs; y-indexeddb package path, no version pinned; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Offline Support, lines 1-44.
sources.observed_operation: y-indexeddb writes changes to local IndexedDB and loads them on the next visit; only latest updates are sent to the network provider; multiple providers can be combined.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Examples target browser IndexedDB; native applications need an environment-appropriate database provider from the ecosystem. Browser page assets need separate offline availability.
sources.applicability: Good web/JS alternative; adds provider/binding work for a Rust desktop UI.

sources.title: Yjs Relative Positions
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs, no version pinned; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Y.RelativePosition, lines 1-20.
sources.observed_operation: A relative position attaches to an element, remains stable under remote insertion, can be encoded, and translates to a current index; resolution returns null if target type is deleted or unavailable.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Applies to text/sequences in the same Yjs document; it does not establish cue-level identity.
sources.applicability: Strong alternate for text-span comments; stable cue IDs remain preferable for whole-cue anchors.

sources.title: ShareDB Introduction
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs, no version pinned; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Introduction/features, lines 35-53.
sources.observed_operation: ShareDB is a Node.js server/client for JSON collaboration; it delegates OT transformation to types and advertises offline change sync upon reconnection and historic versions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Server coordinates/commits; OT semantics depend on registered type plugin.
sources.applicability: Server-authoritative alternative with additional service and app policy needs.

sources.title: ShareDB Reconnecting Client Example
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs, no version pinned; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Client/WebSocket example, lines 83-119.
sources.observed_operation: Reconnects with reconnecting-websocket but sets maxEnqueuedMessages=0 because ShareDB says buffering while the socket is closed has undefined behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Example disables WebSocket buffering and shows server-backed subscribe/submitOp; it is not a durable local outbox implementation.
sources.applicability: Requires separate durable client outbox/replay and server persistence for disconnected rehearsal work.

sources.observed_operation: Shows List insert/delete, MovableList set/move, two replicas making concurrent moves and importing updates; both converge to one deterministic position, with the higher PeerID's move winning in the example.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: List is for insert/delete; simulating move with delete+insert can yield duplicate logical elements under concurrent edits. MovableList has native move/set but costs more; docs estimate about 80% slower encode/decode and 50% more memory for insert/delete-only workloads.

sources.title: Loro Cursor and Stable Positions
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs, no version pinned; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Heading Cursor, lines 70-80 and examples 81-110.
sources.observed_operation: Separately storable cursor identifies a position in Text/List/MovableList; after insert/delete, it resolves to an updated position. Docs demonstrate cursors for comment ranges.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Integer indexes are unstable. When a referenced element is deleted, Loro recalculates the position by replaying relevant history and updates cursor metadata to refer to present elements; longer replay can cost more. JS offsets use UTF-16.
sources.applicability: Useful for optional text-range comments; cue-level comments should use an explicit cue_id rather than sequence indexes.

sources.title: Loro Sync
sources.version_or_commit: Living official docs, no version pinned; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Real-time Collaboration and Sync Strategies, lines 77-120; Import Status/Pending Operations, lines 184-200.
sources.observed_operation: Exports updates from a peer version vector and imports them; same state is reached for the same updates independent of order/duplicates. Import status exposes pending causal dependencies. Regular child containers independently created under one Map key can hide a value; docs recommend ensure_mergeable_* for shared logical keys.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Convergence assumes peers eventually receive the same update set. Non-empty pending ranges mean required dependencies are missing. Conflicting regular child containers under one map key do not both appear as values.
sources.applicability: Supports offline update exchange, durable outbox/relay design, schema initialization, and explicit missing-range recovery.

records.title: Automerge Rust core API
records.released_version_or_commit: Rust crate automerge 0.12.0; docs.rs versioned page. Source commit not inspected.
records.locator: Automerge methods: apply_changes, save, get_heads, set_author; current crate page identifies 0.12.0.
records.review_method: Opened the Rust API documentation; no code executed.
records.observed_operation: apply_changes is idempotent for already-applied changes. save serializes the entirety of a document in compact form. An Author must be set; otherwise Change::author is None.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Idempotence applies to replaying identical changes. A missing author is allowed by default. save is a full-document save, not a transport or durable-write guarantee.
records.applicability: Directly applicable to a Rust+Slint client as the document core. The app still owns local crash-safe persistence, relay authentication, and mapping authenticated crew identities to author metadata.

records.title: Automerge Rust ReadDoc conflict and history API
records.released_version_or_commit: Rust crate automerge 0.12.0.
records.locator: get_all/get_all_at at trait methods; *_at description and get_cursor methods.
records.review_method: Opened the versioned ReadDoc API page and read the relevant method declarations and descriptions.
records.observed_operation: get_all returns all values and operation IDs for a property; get_all_at and other *_at methods read a historical state at ChangeHash heads. get_cursor creates a stable address within a list or text sequence; movement policy handles a referenced item later being removed.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Historical reads need the chosen head set. A cursor addresses a sequence position, not a cue entity; if its referenced item is removed, the MoveCursor policy matters.
records.applicability: Use get_all for field-level conflict candidates and *_at for approved revision materialization. Cue-level comments should still store cue_id; cursors are only a possible optional text-range anchor.

records.title: Automerge Rust sync protocol
records.released_version_or_commit: Rust crate automerge 0.12.0.
records.locator: Sync Protocol opening and example loop.
records.review_method: Opened the Rust sync module documentation; no messages were sent.
records.observed_operation: Each peer maintains a State per peer. The initiator generates the first message, the receiver applies it and generates a reply, and peers exchange messages until neither generates another.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The documented protocol assumes a reliable in-order stream. This is a protocol requirement; after possible loss, the prior state is unsafe to reuse without recovery.
records.applicability: A WebSocket/TCP relay can provide ordered delivery within a connection, but the app must detect disconnect uncertainty and reset/reconcile session state. The reference loop is guidance, not a tested relay.

records.title: Automerge Rust sync State
records.released_version_or_commit: Rust crate automerge 0.12.0.
records.locator: State::encode/decode, new_read_only, read_only and set_read_only descriptions.
records.review_method: Opened the versioned Rust sync State page.
records.observed_operation: State can be encoded and decoded for reuse with the same peer. A read-only State ignores incoming changes while continuing to send its local changes.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Read-only is directional protocol behavior, not a data-store ACL. Persist state only while the peer/session relationship remains valid; if a message could have been lost, issue #1284 and the maintainer require reset.
records.applicability: Can help construct a publish-only client/relay path, but approval records and relay authorization must be separately enforced.

records.title: Rust sync lost-message issue #1284
records.released_version_or_commit: Issue opened 2026-02-13; no target crate version named in the issue. Open, no assignee or linked fix/PR visible at 2026-10-12T01:05:53Z.
records.locator: Issue reproduction steps for offline-generated message and reconnect (lines 243–268); maintainer reply (lines 273–284).
records.review_method: Opened the primary repository issue and read the reproducer and maintainer response.
records.observed_operation: Reporter demonstrates that generating then dropping an unsent sync message before an offline conflicting edit can make reconnect synchronization loop indefinitely; keeping the exact unsent message avoids that reproduction. Maintainer says the protocol requires reliable in-order delivery and sync state must be reset if a message may have been dropped.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The issue is open; it is not evidence that every release fails or that JavaScript has the same behavior. The maintainer explains the required recovery contract but does not supply an application relay implementation.
records.applicability: Direct Rust reconnect risk. Persist local document first; on uncertain disconnect reset/rebuild sync State or preserve the exact in-flight message/state pair; test the reproduction against the selected crate and adapter.

records.title: Automerge conflict behavior (language-neutral behavior described in JS docs)
records.released_version_or_commit: Unversioned current project documentation, accessed 2026-10-12. Rust API cross-check is S02 (0.12.0).
records.locator: Concurrent map assignment example and explanation of getConflicts / multi-value register.
records.review_method: Opened the official Automerge conflict guide.
records.observed_operation: Independent edits to different fields combine. Concurrent writes to one property expose a deterministic visible winner and retain all values for a conflict query. Winner ordering is operation-ID based, not wall-clock latest.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: This page uses the JavaScript getConflicts name and is not Rust API syntax; Rust get_all is documented separately. A later causally dependent assignment resolves the prior property conflict.
records.applicability: Supports a human decision panel for same-field candidates, provided Rust UI uses get_all and explicitly records a user resolution rather than presenting the deterministic winner as approval.

records.title: Automerge collaborative text behavior
records.released_version_or_commit: Unversioned current project documentation; code examples are JavaScript.
records.locator: Collaborative text editing, splice/updateText, frequency caveat.
records.review_method: Opened the official Automerge text guide.
records.observed_operation: Collaborative strings are text sequences. Fine-grained splice edits merge concurrently; updateText can derive changes from a full input value but works best when called frequently, while less frequent whole-value diffs may merge poorly.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: This is a JavaScript UI guide. The native Rust text transaction/update methods and Slint event mapping must be confirmed before implementation.
records.applicability: Cue notes/comments need actual text operations, not blind whole-value replacements. Even a converged text sequence may need a human readability review for overlapping/offline replacements.

records.title: Automerge fine-grained lists and history/size guidance
records.released_version_or_commit: Unversioned current project documentation; current page reviewed 2026-10-12. Related history/performance locator: https://automerge.org/docs/cookbook/modeling-data/.
records.locator: List guide entity-map + ID-list pattern (around lines 116–134); Modeling Data Performance section (around lines 163–168).
records.review_method: Opened the official list and data-modeling guides.
records.observed_operation: The docs advise updating fine-grained entity fields and ID lists instead of replacing an entire nested object. Documents keep their entire change history by default, and the docs recommend workload-specific measurements.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The list examples are JavaScript but illustrate Automerge's data model. History retention means deleted values may remain in the document history unless a separate retention/compaction policy is established.

records.title: WebVTT: The Web Video Text Tracks Format
records.released_version_or_commit: W3C Candidate Recommendation Draft dated 2026-05-20; exact snapshot linked by the page at https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-webvtt1-20260520/; explicitly a draft, not a Recommendation

In-file formatting and layout are a defined subset; cue text includes b/i/u, ruby, voice, language, and text spans. Cue box settings are enumerated. The page warns its current version is a draft that may change.

records.title: Timed Text Markup Language 2 (TTML2)
records.released_version_or_commit: W3C Recommendation, 2018-11-08; stable reference; page points readers to errata
records.locator: §5 profiling; §8 content and timing vocabulary; §10 styling; §12 timing/timeContainer; §14 metadata and xml:lang
records.observed_operation: Opened the Recommendation and inspected its status, profile model, timeContainer values, xml:lang examples, and style/region definitions.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: TTML supports explicit content/processor profiles; validation and effective behavior depend on the profile. Timed children can be locally parallel or sequential. Language can be inherited or specified per element. Region and style features exceed WebVTT's in-file cue markup, but processors may not implement every profile or property.
records.applicability: Rich interchange option and exact timing/style source; adapters must name a profile and report unsupported features rather than claim all TTML2 documents round-trip.

records.observed_operation: Opened the IETF Standards Track text and inspected its schema/table of contents and track/attachment sections.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Matroska models a single audiovisual Segment with typed tracks, timing and track metadata; it also supports attachments. Track flags are selection hints, and actual selection is player-dependent. Text codec and timestamp rules remain codec-specific.
records.applicability: Practical single-media-file alternative with multiple tracks and attached resources; not itself a complete authoring-package model or guarantee of identical rendering.

sources.title: WebVTT: The Web Video Text Tracks Format
sources.version_commit: W3C Candidate Recommendation Draft, 2026-05-20; explicitly work in progress
sources.observed_operation: Opened W3C published-version page and inspected status, cue examples, cue ordering/timing, normalization, cue settings and render behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: One data kind per WebVTT file. Cue start offsets are nondecreasing and each cue end is after its start; examples permit overlapping cues. Processing must not normalize Unicode. Rendering/styling support is user-agent limited; regions default to three lines and can clip overflow.
sources.applicability: Per-track timed-text interchange, overlap semantics, rich cue text retention, and export loss reporting. Because this is a CR Draft, treat its status as draft and verify target interoperability before shipping.

sources.locator: Abstract and status; §5 profiles; time expressions and timing parameters; §6 styling vocabulary
sources.observed_operation: Opened the pinned Recommendation and reviewed the abstract/status; inspected the latest-linked document for profiles and timing semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: TTML is timed text intended for interchange among authoring systems. Profile declarations constrain vocabulary/processor behavior. Time expression meaning depends on governing time base, with media as default when unspecified in the inspected specification.
sources.applicability: Richer timed-text alternative; profile-specific implementation and round-trip tests are required. Do not claim every TTML profile or extension is supported.

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Timed text supports different clock/frame/offset expressions; frame interpretation depends on frame-rate parameters and time base. Draft status is not equivalent to an endorsed final Recommendation.
sources.applicability: Discovery of timing/profile complexity and candidate adapter coverage; not sufficient alone to promise stable 2e support.

sources.title: Tokio spawn_blocking
sources.version_or_commit: Tokio 1.53.2; crate feature rt
sources.locator: Function description, cancellation and runtime shutdown sections
sources.observed_operation: A blocking closure uses a blocking pool with a high configured ceiling; started closures cannot be aborted, and shutdown may wait indefinitely.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Use only for bounded work that eventually finishes; unsuitable as the only containment mechanism for hostile/hung parsers.
sources.applicability: Tokio Rust apps using spawn_blocking; useful for bounded trusted blocking work, not forceful parser cancellation.

sources.version_or_commit: tokio-util 0.7.20 stable release; latest docs at capture
sources.locator: child_token, cancel, cancelled, cancellation safety
sources.observed_operation: cancel wakes waiting tasks and propagates to child tokens; cancellation itself is not atomic until return; the future is cancel-safe.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Cooperative async cancellation and job-scoped token hierarchy; does not terminate native/blocking code.
sources.applicability: Tokio async tasks and cooperative worker protocols; not an OS process kill.

sources.title: Tokio process Command

sources.locator: kill_on_drop, process_group, spawn cancellation sections

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Async child supervision; dropping a handle is not a portable process-tree kill.
sources.applicability: Rust/Tokio app-owned child renderers; process-group API is Unix-only and does not itself apply a sandbox.

sources.title: Rust std::process::Child

sources.title: Tokio Semaphore
sources.version_or_commit: Tokio 1.53.2 stable release; latest docs at capture
sources.locator: Fairness and acquire_many sections
sources.observed_operation: Permits are FIFO; acquire_many at the front can block a later smaller acquisition despite available permits.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Use as a running-work cap behind one priority dispatcher; avoid using FIFO permit arrival as class priority.
sources.applicability: Tokio execution-slot accounting; use behind an app-owned dispatcher, not as the priority queue.

sources.locator: Managing Processes in Jobs; Job Limits; tree management

sources.applicability: Windows-only process grouping, accounting, limits, and termination; no filesystem/network sandbox guarantee.

sources.applicability: Linux kernels with required Landlock ABI/rights; runtime feature probing and no_new_privs are necessary for an unprivileged launch.

sources.title: Landlock: unprivileged access control
sources.version_or_commit: Linux kernel documentation dated August 2026; ABI and rights depend on running kernel
sources.locator: Defining/enforcing a policy and ABI compatibility, lines 62–106, 176–228; network rights lines 23–26; descriptor semantics lines 270–282
sources.observed_operation: Unprivileged enforcement requires no_new_privs; applications query ABI and mask unsupported rights. TCP network rules begin at ABI 4 and UDP at ABI 10. Some rights are bound to opened file descriptors; preconnected datagram sockets are not constrained by later IPC scoping.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Only operations covered by handled rights are denied by default; old ABIs lack later network controls; already-open descriptors and sockets require deliberate handling.
sources.applicability: Optional Linux filesystem/network sandbox backend only when runtime ABI, rights, descriptor state, and policy are sufficient.

sources.locator: Thumb::MTime / Thumb::Size metadata and Detect Modifications, lines 180–185 and 261–278
sources.observed_operation: The standard stores mtime in seconds and recommends checking size; it warns that multiple files can share the one-second mtime and that mtime alone can leave an incorrect thumbnail.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: This is a cache interoperability/freshness standard, not a generic thumbnail-service API; size is an additional check, not proof of identical content.
sources.applicability: Linux/XDG thumbnail cache precedent; does not substantiate the draft's generic Linux user thumbnail service alternative.

sources.title: Zotero attachmentPreview.js
sources.version_or_commit: Zotero v7.0.12; pinned commit 6af5a484fd6688aab23150938d69df42dfca10e4
sources.locator: _processTask and Promise.race, lines 2050–2117; _processRender and _tryAbortRender, lines 2131–2225
sources.observed_operation: Latest-task bookkeeping is processed in order on the normal path; each render races against a 3-second delay, after which flags are reset regardless. A losing render promise is not cancelled by Promise.race. Item-ID equality is checked before and after awaited render work.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A UI component/renderer precedent in Zotero 7.0.12, not an OS process boundary. The 3-second timeout frees bookkeeping, not necessarily the underlying render.
sources.applicability: Supports latest-task coalescing and an item-ID acceptance check; does not support an unconditional claim that timed-out work is serialized or terminated.

reviser_recheck.locator: Kernel docs, Landlock rules and backward compatibility lines 25-33, 63-105; network rights lines 438-456; descriptor semantics lines 268, 370; unprivileged enforcement lines 206-216; support lines 877-883
reviser_recheck.observed_operation: Rechecked current kernel documentation. TCP bind/connect restrictions require ABI 4; UDP bind and connect/send restrictions require ABI 10. The documented network rules cover TCP/UDP ports and the handled rights must be explicit for default denial. Files opened before sandboxing remain outside path restrictions; a previously connected socket can send without the cited abstract-UNIX-socket scope restriction.
reviser_recheck.governing_condition_default_exception: A runtime ABI query and rights mask are necessary but not sufficient for an asserted no-network policy. For documented TCP/UDP denial, require ABI 10, handle all four rights (TCP bind/connect, UDP bind/connect-send) with no allow rules, set no_new_privs for an unprivileged launch, and close/avoid inherited network descriptors. Landlock alone is not a general network firewall; fail closed or use another qualified control if the policy cannot be established.
reviser_recheck.applicability: Linux filesystem/port sandbox candidate only after per-kernel policy and descriptor tests; selected read-only input capability is an intentional exception to general filesystem restrictions.

reviser_recheck.observed_operation: Rechecked the pinned file at the same commit. It coalesces to the most recent task and waits for current render/discard flags for up to 300×10 ms, then races render/discard against a 3-second delay and resets bookkeeping flags.
